articles.title: Media silence as Kushner's $2B tie to Saudis slips under cover of Trump deal: analyst
articles.description: White House spokesperson Karoline Leavitt should be fielding questions about Jared Kushner 's $2 billion tie to Saudi Arabia , a media expert fumed Thursday. Judd Legum, founder of the Substack Popular.info , took to social media to share his disgust after Leavitt was grilled about President Donald Trump 's controversial nuclear deal at a White House press conference. His frustration appeared in the form of a list of news outlets that covered the US-Saudi nuclear deal without mentioning that Jared Kushner, Trump’s senior White House aide, is getting paid by the Saudi government." Legum's list included The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, Associated Press, Reuters, CNN, NBC, ABC, CBS, The Guardian, Semafor, The Washington Post, Fox News, The New York Post, BBC, Newsweek, and MS NOW. Kushner launched his private equity firm Affinity Partners shortly after leaving the White House in 2021 after Trump's first administration, reports show. The Florida-based company received a $2 billion investment from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, multiple reports show. The deal drew scrutiny from ethics watchdogs given Kushner's role shaping U.S.-Saudi relations, including his involvement in defending MBS after the killing of Washington Post journalist Jamal Khashoggi. On his Substack , Legum dubbed the coverage, "A media blackout for Kushner’s corruption."

articles.title: Pete Hegseth's shaky budget claims called out on MS NOW: 'Math doesn't add up'
articles.description: Sen. Tim Kaine (D-VA) cut through Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth's budget demands on MS NOW Wednesday — and said he smelled a rat in the whole thing. This comes as President Donald Trump continues to try to prosecute his war in Iran , without any clear plan to achieve a lasting objective. Trump, Kaine noted to anchor Jacob Soboroff, "is asking for a 40 percent increase in the Pentagon's budget over last year, with no guardrails, in the middle of an illegal war, and coming to us and asking for an additional $67 billion to fund a war that is illegal, and that's deeply unpopular with the American public." Congress, he said, should find its spine and force an end to the war instead. Soboroff noted that reports indicate the U.S. is low on interceptor missiles , and being forced to disclose a growing number of casualties for American troops. With that in mind, he continued, "is a standalone defense spending bill something that you would support?" "Well, when the Pentagon says they're running out of money, they neglect to tell you something: that the reconciliation bill that passed last year, that gave $153 billion extra dollars to the Pentagon, $89 billion of that has not yet been obligated," said Kaine. So when Hegseth demands another $67 billion round, Kaine continued, "What about the $89 billion you have sitting over there that we gave you last year that you haven't even spent?" "This math doesn't add up," Kaine concluded. And bottom line, he refused to commit more money to "an illegal war that's deeply unpopular with Americans that President Trump never should have started." - YouTube www.youtube.com
